The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 02.07.2022.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 02.07.2022 at about 9.45 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Tumakuru Traffic Police station at Ashoka Road, Health Canteen Cross, the petitioner was proceeding to KSRTC bus stand to board the bus in order to go to his village, at that time the driver KSRTC bus bearing Reg. NO.KA-06-F-1173 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner.

Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and the left side back wheel of the bus ran over on both the legs of the claimant and thereby he sustained grievous crush injuries to both legs and all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to General Hospital, Tumakuru and later he was shifted to Aditya Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre, B.H. Road, Tumakuru wherein he was admitted as inpatient and the left leg of the petitioner was amputed.

entities.text: Aditya Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre, B.H. Road
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He has spent more than Rs.5,00,000/- towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,

Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as a Loader of vegetable to Lorry under package system and was earning Rs.1,500/-
per day and in week days he used to earn Rs.2,000/- to Rs.3,000/- per day.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.

The respondent No.1 is the owner and internal insurer of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.
NO.KA-06-F-1173 and respondent No.2 is the driver of the offending bus, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel, but the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the tribunal, hence, placed exparte.
The 1st respondent has appeared and filed written statement by denying that the accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg. NO.KA-06-F-1173.

Further contended that the bus was proceeding from Tumkur Depot No.2 towards bus stand,
Tumkur and it was driven by its driver in a slow and cautious manner and while took turn towards bus station, Tumkur, petitioner/pedestrian consumed alcohol without following traffic rules and regulations came in zig-zag motion, lost control over himself while crossing the road and fell down on the road, his leg touched to left side back wheel of the said bus, suffered injuries.
Further denied the age, avocation, alleged disability and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent prays to dismiss the petition against it.

sentences.text:
4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-F-1173 by its driver, in RTA took place on 02.07.2022 at about 9.45 p.m near Ashok road, health Canteen road cross, national High way-33, Tumkuru District?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
3 . What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 22.
Also examined two witnesses as PW.2 & 3 and got marked documents at Ex.P23 to 27.

First respondent examined the driver of the offending KSRTC bus/2nd respondent as RW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R1 to 5.
6.
Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, order sheet in CC No.9273/2022, charge sheet, spot mahazar along with sketch, seizure mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate and statement of witnesses, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 9.
9.
To prove his case, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No. KA-06-F- 1173.
The Ex.P2 first information is lodged by the relative of the petitioner by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the respondent No.2.
On the basis of Ex.P2 first information the FIR as per Ex.P1 is registered.
10. After registering the FIR spot mahazar and rough sketch is conducted by the IO as per Ex.P.5.
On perusal of the said Ex.P5 the accident is in the left side road in which the petitioner was walking.
The Ex.P6 is the seizure report and Ex.P7 is IMV report wherein no fresh visible damages were found on the offending vehicle.

It is very important to note that the accident is not disputed by the Rangaiah vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90616312/
3 respondent No.1.

entities.text: Rangaiah vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The fact of accident is admitted by the respondent No.1 and also the RW.1 who was the driver of the offending bus at the time of accident.
Only the fact of negligence is disputed by the respondents.

By keeping this in background if we were perused the available materials on record and also on the basis of the evidence of RW.1 i.e., the driver of the KSRTC bus, admittedly the left side back tyre was ran on the both the legs of the petitioner.
As per the mahazar the accident in the left side of the road.
As per the evidence of RW.1 while coming out from the KSRTC depot and while entering into KSRTC bus stand the accident is caused.
Admittedly the backside tyre was ran over on the both the legs of the petitioner.
The accident spot is near to the turning and also the left side portion of the road.
Thus it evidentiates that the driver of the offending bus was negligent and caused the accident.
The respondent even though has taken the defence that the petitioner was under the influence of alcohol, no evidence is placed in support of their defence.
The Ex.
P.8 the wound certificate wherein it does not reflects that the petitioner was under the influence of alcohol.
In fact the Ex.P.8 discloses that both the legs of the petitioner has got crush injuries.
Ex.P19 is the discharge summary discloses that there is a crush injury of left leg and non viable crush injury to right heel.
During the course of treatment the disarticulation of right knee was done.
The disarticulation means the separation of two bones at their joint, either traumatically by way of injury or by a surgeon during arthroplasty or amputation.
This shows that the bus ran over the right knee of the petitioner which once again shows that the offending bus was negligent and ran over on the petitioner.
By this it can be held that the negligent is on the part of driver of the offending bus and no grounds are made out to accept defence of the respondents.

11. The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 relied on the judgment reported on the 1994 ACJ 1303 of Hon'ble High Court of Orissa between Mathaji Bewa & others V/s Hemanth Kumar Jena wherein it is held as follows:
"6.

entities.text: Mathaji Bewa & others V/s Hemanth Kumar Jena
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the rival submissions of the parties, the first question that arises for consideration is whether the Tribunal was justified in holding that the deceased was travelling on the offending truck as a passenger and succumbed to the injury on account of the accident of the truck in question.
The sole basis for the Tribunal to come to the aforesaid conclusion is the contents of a charge-sheet filed in the criminal case.
The contents of a charge-sheet cannot possibly be treated as an evidence in the claim proceedings.
The Tribunal obviously committed gross error of law in relying upon the said charge-sheet to come to the conclusion that the deceased was travelling on the truck as a passenger.
On the other hand, the positive evidence of the claimants that the deceased was a pedestrian and the truck came and knocked him down has not been impeached in any manner by way of cross-examination.
There was no justification on the part of the Tribunal to ignore that evidence of the claimants.
In the aforesaid premises, the finding of the Tribunal that the deceased was travelling on the truck cannot be sustained and the said finding is accordingly set aside.
On the evidence on record, it must be held that the deceased was a pedestrian and while going on the road, the offending truck came and knocked him down".

By relying on the about quoted judgment the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 argued that the contents of charge sheet cannot be relied by the tribunal and the evidence lead by the parties has Rangaiah vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90616312/
4 to be considered independently.

entities.text: Rangaiah vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No doubt that the contents of charge sheet cannot be considered as a conclusive evidence and proof while deciding the fact of negligence.
Evidence lead by the parties has to be considered while fixing the fact of negligence.
In this case the respondent except examining the driver of offending bus has not produced any other evidence to disbelieve the contents of mahazar which shows the exact spot of the accident.
It is very important to note that the accident spot as shown in the Ex.P.5 mahazar is also not disputed by the respondents.
The respondents contended that the petitioner was under the influence of alcohol and he himself by his negligence came under the left side portion of the bus.
But to accept the said defence no piece of evidence is produced by the respondent.
No evidence is available to hold that the petitioner was under the influence of alcohol.
12. Further as admitted by the RW.1 the charge sheet as per Ex.P.4 is filed against him.
If the petitioner was under the influence of alcohol why the same was not intimated to the police or to the hospital authorities is not explained by the respondents.
The Ex.P.8 wound certificate discloses that the petitioner was bought to the hospital by the driver of the offending bus.
The Ex.P23 is MLC register extract wherein the said document also not supports the defence of the respondents.
When the driver of the offending bus himself admitted the petitioner to the hospital, he could have inform the hospital authorities that the petitioner was under the influence of alcohol.
The RW.1 produced Ex.R3 statement given by him in his departmental enquiry.
Only in the said statement he has stated that the petitioner was under the influence of alcohol.
The said document is an internal statement given by the driver to his department.
The said document and the evidence of respondents is not supported with the any other evidence.
No grounds are made to accept that the petitioner was under the influence of alcohol.
13. Another defence is taken by the respondent No.1 that as the petitioner was crossing the road it is expected that even he was the negligent and the contributory negligence has to be considered.

In this regard the respondent relied on the judgment reported in ILR 1988 KAR 1934 of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka between Sri Narasimhaiah V/s The General Manager & another wherein it is held as follows:
7.

entities.text: Narasimhaiah V/s The General Manager & another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant in this case was a pedestrian who virtually walked into the path of the vehicle and got injured.

There is a wrong notion which prevails that pedestrains have the birth-right to wander around the stroll on the roads according to their whims and fancies and that even if they make every effort to get run over, that the vehicle drivers are supposed to still try and save them.
It has been pointed out in this judgment that the rules of the road require pedestrians to avoid strolling on to the road and that the roads can be crossed only at designated places.

A breach of these rules immediately holds the pedestrain liable for negligence and if it is demonstrated that the injury of death occurred due to the negligence of the pedestrain, the driver of the vehicle, the owner and the insurer would then be entitled to disclaim their liability.
This is an aspect of the law that has been grossly overlooked and which requires to be very clearly restated and specifically brought to the notice of the public.

Rangaiah vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90616312/
5

entities.text: Rangaiah vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The present accident took place on one of the busy roads in the city of Bangalore and the evidence indicates that people were indiscriminately walking about on the road virtually between the vehicles that were moving regardless of any concern for safety.

Where a pedestrain demonstrates suicidal tendencies by behaving in this manner, he will be precluded from then holding others liable if he gets injured or killed and it is very necessary that this message goes out loud and clear.

In the present instance where the driver of the vehicle and the injured appellant are both demonstrated to have been negligent, the first one for the manner in which the truck was being driven and the second one for having crossed the road at a point where he should not have done, this Court has had to evaluate the degrees of negligence for purposes of deciding whether the injured should be entitled to compensation and if so, how much.
The degree of negligence on the part of the pedestrain having been of a relatively lower order, the Court has limited the compensation payable to the extent of GO of the amount computed.
In cases of proven negligence however, the compensation awarded could be much lower or even nothing at all.
It is pathetic that there is virtually zero level of traffic management in this city but it is not too late for the department to make a beginning.

The first step would necessarily be through a virtually educative process whereby all persons using the roads from the drivers down to pedestrians are informed through a sustained media campaign as to what are the rules of the road, what is the discipline that is required to be observed and above all, the penalises for breaching these which could end up in not only the payment of heavy fines but the forfeiture of compensation in cases of damage or injury.
It is unfortunate to say the least that this indiscipline has been permitted to grow to a level of uncontrollable chaos.

If the Union territory of Delhi and the State of Maharastra, to name just two, have been able to bring about a semblance of order on their roads, there is no reason why it cannot be done in this state.
The authorities will have to first shed their indolence, learn what their duties are and start doing them for a change.
In this case as per the mahazar the accident spot is in the left side of the road.
As admitted by the PW.1 he was trying to cross the road.
As per the mahzar in the accident place the divider is opened and the pedestrians ought to have cross the road in the said place.
Near to the bus stand the driver of the heavy vehicles ought to be vigilant.
As the petitioner was trying to cross the road in the place where the divider is open and meant for crossing of the road by the pedestrians.
Hence, in my humble opinion the above quoted judgment is not applicable to the present case.
Accordingly no other grounds are made out to show the contributory negligence by the petitioner.
14. As per Ex.P.5 spot mahazar the accident spot is within the four feet of the road edge which shows that the driver of the KSRTC bus rash and negiigent.
15. No doubt that the pedestrians has to cross the road in the place where it is meant for pedestrian crossing.

In this case, as per Ex.P5- spot mahazar and rough sketch the divider and the road along with footpath is open in the accident spot and the pedestrians has to cross the road in the said place only which once again shows the negligence of the driver of the offending bus.
16. As per well settled position of law the standard of proof in claim petition like present one, is only preponderance of probabilities.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 02.07.2022 which is caused by the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA- 06-F-1173 which belongs to the respondent No.1.
There is no reasons to discard the evidence of petitioner.

In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary Rangaiah vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90616312/
6 but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.

sentences.text: Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
17.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the vehicle belongs to respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 50 years.
In the Aadhaar card produced at Ex.P-20 the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 01.01.1972.
The accident took place in the year 2022.
Hence, as on the date of accident, the petitioner was aged about 50 years.

As per the discharge summary produced at Ex.P19 the petitioner sustained crush injury to left leg,
non viable crush injury right heel.

He underwent disarticulation of right knee on 04.07.2022,
debridement left heel and secondary closure of stamp done on 13.07.2022.
As per the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.9 the petitioner sustained grievous injuries to his both legs and one simple injury.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.75,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P17 amounting to Rs.1,91,789/-.
These bills are also supported with the case records produced by the PW.2 and no grounds are made out to disbelieving these bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitle for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same i.e., Rs.1,91,800/-.
d) Loss of future income due to disability To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner examined Dr.Praveen H.V. Orthopaedic Surgeon as PW.3,

through him clinical notes,
case sheet and X-ray are marked at Ex.P25 to 27.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained crush injury to left leg with neurovascular injury and he underwent surgery.
PW.3 examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
As per PW.3 the petitioner suffered permanent disability of 75% to left lower limb and 25% to the whole body.
As discussed above, the evidence of PW.3 shows that the condition of the petitioner he has to depend on other due to disarticulation amputation through knee for left lower limb.
The petitioner has to walk with external support and also the stand and to move the petitioner is in need of external support.
The said fact is established by the evidence of doctor PW.3 and also Ex.P.21 & 22 photographs.
The age of the petitioner has to be considered to assess whether the petitioner can live independently without any one support with the left leg below knee amputation.
Thus, it can be construed that the petitioner has to be depend on others and his avocational disability has to be considered at 100%.

In this regard, I rely on the reportable decision, in Civil Appeal No.2476/2019 in the case of M.R.Krishamurthi V/s New India Assurance Company Ltd., decided on 05.03.2019, the Hon'ble supreme court has held as follows, "We may now summarize the principles discussed above:
Rangaiah vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90616312/
7

entities.text: M.R.Krishamurthi V/s New India Assurance Company Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (i) All injuries (or permanent disabilities arising from injuries), do not result in loss of earning capacity.
(ii) The percentage of permanent disability with reference to the whole body of a person, cannot be assumed to be the percentage of loss of earning capacity.

To put it differently, the percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability (except in a few cases, where the Tribunal on the basis of evidence, concludes that the percentage of loss of earning capacity is the same as the percentage of permanent disability).
(iii) The doctor who treated an injured claimant or who examined him subsequently to assess the extent of his permanent disability can give evidence only in regard to the extent of permanent disability.
The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence in entirety.

(iv) The same permanent disability may result in different percentages of loss of earning capacity in different persons, depending upon the nature of profession,
occupation or job, age, education and other factors."
A perusal of the injuries sustained, treatment taken and in view of the citation referred above, it is considered that though the petitioner is having 70% permanent physical disability, his avocational disability is 100% because the evidence of Pw.2 is clear that the petitioner is unable to attend his day to day work without assistance and unable to walk unassisted.
This situation is nothing but making this tribunal to hold that the petitioner is unable to earn or to live independently hence, this disability is considered at 100%.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '13'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.15,500/- X 12 X 13 X 100% =Rs.24,18,000/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per Ex.P19 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 20 days and the injuries sustained by him grievous in nature.
As per the wound certificate marked at Ex.P8 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
For the reasons discussed above, is already held that the petitioner is suffering with 100% disability and unable to attend his own works without the assistance of others.
This making this tribunal consider that the petitioner is in need of an attendant through out his life time.
The services of the family members cannot be considered graciously.
The petitioner should not be looked into as a burden to the family.

Rangaiah vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90616312/
8

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No evidence is lead by the petitioner to show that he has engaged an attendant by paying money.

In Kajal Vs. Jaidish Chand reported in 2020 SCC Online SC 127, it is held that it would be appropriate to adopt the system of multiplier to award the compensation under the head 'Attendant Charges' as the claimant would require the care of an attendant for the rest of his life.

entities.text: Kajal Vs. Jaidish Chand reported in 2020 SCC Online SC 127
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such this court is of the opinion that the claimant is entitled for 'Attendant Charges' at the rate of Rs.100 per day which is quantified at Rs.4,68,000/- (Rs.100 x 30 x 12 x 13).
Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award Rs.4,68,000/- towards attendant charges.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived his of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.
h)Towards future medical expenses: No evidence is lead by the petitioner by showing the future medical expenses, hence, the petitioner is not entitled for the compensation under this head.
i) Towards Loss of Income during the laid up period: The disability of the petitioner is considered at 100% as such no separate compensation awarded under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a) Towards pain and agony Rs. 75,000/-
b) Towards medical expenses Rs. 1,91,800/-
c) Towards loss of income NIL d) Towards disability 24,18,000/-
e) Towards food, nourishment  and conveyance Rs. 20,000/-
f) Towards attendant charges Rs. 4,68,000/-
g) Towards loss of amenities Rs. 50,000/-
h) Towards future medical  expenses NIL  _______________  Total Rs. 32,22,800/-
18. Liability:-
As discussed above, the petitioner successfully proved the negligence on the part of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-06-F-1173.
The amount of compensation which is the petitioner is entitled
is also discussed now.

The last point Rangaiah vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90616312/
9 for consideration in this petition is who has to pay the compensation going to be awarded in this petition.
19. Regarding the liability, the respondent No.1 is owner and internal insurer of the offending bus.
No other grounds are made out to disentitle the petitioner in claiming the compensation.
As such the respondent No.1 has to pay the compensation along with interest.

The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., Accordingly, this issue answered partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
20.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.32,22,800/- (Rupees Thirty two lakhs twenty two thousand eight hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of total compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 50% of the same to be released in favour of petitioner through E- payment on his proper identification and remaining 50% to be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years, in his name.

Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 02.07.2022.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent prays to dismiss the petition against it.
opennyai_summary.issue:
4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-F-1173 by its driver, in RTA took place on 02.07.2022 at about 9.45 p.m near Ashok road, health Canteen road cross, national High way-33, Tumkuru District?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
3 . What order or award?
In view of the rival submissions of the parties, the first question that arises for consideration is whether the Tribunal was justified in holding that the deceased was travelling on the offending truck as a passenger and succumbed to the injury on account of the accident of the truck in question.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Evidence lead by the parties has to be considered while fixing the fact of negligence.
In this case the respondent except examining the driver of offending bus has not produced any other evidence to disbelieve the contents of mahazar which shows the exact spot of the accident.
No evidence is available to hold that the petitioner was under the influence of alcohol.
If the petitioner was under the influence of alcohol why the same was not intimated to the police or to the hospital authorities is not explained by the respondents.
No grounds are made to accept that the petitioner was under the influence of alcohol.

Where a pedestrain demonstrates suicidal tendencies by behaving in this manner, he will be precluded from then holding others liable if he gets injured or killed and it is very necessary that this message goes out loud and clear.
In the present instance where the driver of the vehicle and the injured appellant are both demonstrated to have been negligent, the first one for the manner in which the truck was being driven and the second one for having crossed the road at a point where he should not have done, this Court has had to evaluate the degrees of negligence for purposes of deciding whether the injured should be entitled to compensation and if so, how much.
The degree of negligence on the part of the pedestrain having been of a relatively lower order, the Court has limited the compensation payable to the extent of GO of the amount computed.
In cases of proven negligence however, the compensation awarded could be much lower or even nothing at all.
The first step would necessarily be through a virtually educative process whereby all persons using the roads from the drivers down to pedestrians are informed through a sustained media campaign as to what are the rules of the road, what is the discipline that is required to be observed and above all, the penalises for breaching these which could end up in not only the payment of heavy fines but the forfeiture of compensation in cases of damage or injury.
In this case as per the mahazar the accident spot is in the left side of the road.
As per the mahzar in the accident place the divider is opened and the pedestrians ought to have cross the road in the said place.
As the petitioner was trying to cross the road in the place where the divider is open and meant for crossing of the road by the pedestrians.
16. As per well settled position of law the standard of proof in claim petition like present one, is only preponderance of probabilities.
All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 02.07.2022 which is caused by the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA- 06-F-1173 which belongs to the respondent No.1.
There is no reasons to discard the evidence of petitioner.
This situation is nothing but making this tribunal to hold that the petitioner is unable to earn or to live independently hence, this disability is considered at 100%.
As per the wound certificate marked at Ex.P8 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
The services of the family members cannot be considered graciously.
The petitioner should not be looked into as a burden to the family.

19. Regarding the liability, the respondent No.1 is owner and internal insurer of the offending bus.

ISSUE NO.3:
20.
For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.32,22,800/- (Rupees Thirty two lakhs twenty two thousand eight hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Out of total compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 50% of the same to be released in favour of petitioner through E- payment on his proper identification and remaining 50% to be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years, in his name.
